typography.strategy: The Swiss Brutalist mixed with Technical Telemetry

headings.family: Cabinet Grotesk, Oswald, or a strong Display Sans (font-sans)
headings.style: Massive scale (text-7xl to text-9xl+ for years), font-black, tracking-tighter, leading-none. Years act as background graphic elements.
headings.usage: Used for the active season year and monumental titles.

body.family: Inter or standard sans but kept minimal.
body.style: text-sm to text-base, high contrast, clean.

data_telemetry.family: JetBrains Mono, Roboto Mono, or IBM Plex Mono (font-mono)
data_telemetry.usage: Used for stats (Wins, Poles), coordinates, lap times, and location lists.

rules: Never use pure black or generic gray gradients. Introduce texture/noise.
Team accent is strictly for interaction colors (active state on timeline, hover).
Championship rank defines the semantic color of the main year typography and stat highlights.

layouts.strategy: Cinematic Museum Installation - No Hard Splits

desktop.structure: Full-width background image with an organic, feathered alpha-mask. The left side (0-60%) shows the image clearly. The right side (40-100%) applies a complex CSS mask (mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, black, transparent)) or a noise-layered backdrop filter so the image dissolves into the data canvas. NO rectangular cards.
desktop.layering: Layer 0: Authentic full-bleed image. Layer 1: Dark noise/fade gradient dissolving left-to-right. Layer 2: Massive overlapping typography (Year) spanning the seam. Layer 3: Telemetry UI and stats.

mobile.structure: Vertical stacking but with deep layering. Image at the top dissolving into the bottom half where data lives.
mobile.layering: Image fades out via linear-gradient to the bottom. Stats overlap the bottom edge of the image fade.

telemetry_identity: Ghost Racing Line: A subtle SVG path snaking down the right side, resembling an F1 track or telemetry graph, with a very low opacity (10-20%).
Scanning Beam: Framer Motion element sweeping vertically across the stats, similar to a radar or wind-tunnel laser.
Lap-Sector Marks: Small 1px lines or ticks along the ghost path denoting key points (Wins, Poles).
Coordinates: Display real-world coordinates of key circuits in tiny mono font as decorative anchors (e.g., 52.0786° N, 1.0169° W).
blending: Eliminate the hard seam using `mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, black 40%, transparent 90%)` on the full-screen image.
Use `backdrop-blur-md` on specific stat areas combined with `bg-black/20` to maintain readability without solid borders.
Mix blend modes (`mix-blend-overlay`, `mix-blend-screen`) on the huge Year typography to interact with the F1 imagery.

motion.strategy: Sleek and highly dynamic, but constrained for performance (transform/opacity only).
elements: Active-season navigation (prev/next) triggers slide/fade transitions on stats and image using Framer Motion (`initial={{ opacity: 0, x: 20 }}`).
Reduced motion support: `useReducedMotion` must disable the scanning beam and slide effects, reverting to simple opacity fades.

accessibility: Ensure contrast ratios (WCAG AA). If stats sit over an image, apply text-shadows or a localized dark radial-gradient behind the text.
Support keyboard navigation (ArrowLeft/ArrowRight) for season changes.
instructions_to_main_agent: Refactor the Timeline chapter layout to remove the hard left/right vertical split. Do not use standard card containers.
Implement the 'hybrid dissolve' effect: Make the background image span 100% width but use `mask-image` or layered gradients to smoothly transition it into a dark, textured area on the right.
Add 'restrained telemetry' visual elements (SVG ghost paths, mono-font coordinates, small lap-sector ticks) to the data panel area.
Integrate Framer Motion for a subtle scanning beam effect (opacity and transform only) and season transitions.
Layer massive, bold year numbers that overlap the transition zone between image and data.
Retain all existing functionality: active-only DOM rendering, Silverstone 3D camera mathematical precision, and exact `data-testid` mapping.
Apply team accent colors to interaction states and championship semantic colors to stat highlights.
Ensure responsive design follows the specific desktop (1920x800) and mobile (390x844) layering rules.
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT: Avoid the 'AI slop' aesthetic: No generic centered layouts, simplistic gradients, or uniform card styling.
Use 2-3x more spacing than typical for a luxurious, monumental feel.
Create depth through layered z-index hierarchy and glass-morphism (blur).
Never use `transition: all`. Target specific properties.
Do not center-align the main app container.
Every interaction needs micro-animations (hover states, focus).
Never use AI emoji characters for icons.
For icons, utilize Lucide-react or Phosphor Icons as appropriate.
Always maintain strict testing attributes: `data-testid` is mandatory for all buttons, links, form inputs, and key data elements.
DO NOT use complete `transparent` background in overlays or headers where content sits underneath.
